column1: # Injected-transport wiring and expectation, for every case whose manifest `source` is
# `http` — and for no other case.
# Columns: case <TAB> stop-handling <TAB> on-first-post <TAB> posts
#   stop-handling  honours  the transport polls HttpRequest::stop and abandons the
#                           exchange on a fired signal — what a transport CAN do
#                  ignores  the transport never reads HttpRequest::stop at all — what a
#                           transport that cannot abandon an in-flight exchange does
#   on-first-post  nothing  the exchange has no effect on the caller's signal
#                  cancel   the exchange cancels the caller's cancellation flag, standing
#                           in for a host that cancels while the evaluator is blocked
#                           inside the transport and can poll nothing
#   posts          the exact number of exchanges the transport must be asked to perform
# `posts` is DERIVED by the corpus regeneration step and re-checked on every run. It is
# the observation that separates "the request was prevented" from "the request was made
# and its answer discarded", which no governor evidence can distinguish.
